title: Integrative network toxicology and machine learning approach identifies potential molecular targets linking Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate exposure to atherosclerosis
content:
Abstract
Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure has been associated with cardiovascular risk, but its molecular links with atherosclerosis remain unclear. We integrated network toxicology, human atherosclerosis transcriptomics, WGCNA, machine learning, SHAP analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and HUVEC validation to identify candidate molecular associations between DEHP and atherosclerosis. Integration of predicted DEHP-associated targets with GSE43292 transcriptomic data identified 56 candidate genes enriched mainly in immune, inflammatory, and leukocyte-migration pathways. A Stepglm–Elastic Net classifier selected using performance across three datasets achieved an AUC of 0.958 in the pooled evaluation of GSE40231 and GSE57691. SHAP analysis prioritized SLCO2A1, TNFSF10, PIM2, CYBB, and STK10, while docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations supported potential structural compatibility with DEHP. In HUVECs, acute DEHP exposure reduced cell viability and migration, increased ROS and MDA, decreased SOD activity, and upregulated the five prioritized genes. These findings provide hypothesis-generating evidence for candidate molecular links between DEHP-associated endothelial injury and atherosclerosis-related biology, although causal relationships require further validation.
